description: Mean absolute error against known synthetic current skill, in 0–100 points. Lower is better. No truth labels are passed to a scoring function.

results.name: Different skills, no systematic reviewer bias
results.note: Tests whether adjustment introduces error when it is unnecessary.

results.name: Harsh and generous reviewers
results.note: Reviewer offsets affect every colleague, independently of their skill.

results.name: Friendship and dislike specific to each pair
results.note: Pair effects are not assumed to be reviewer severity.

results.name: Reviewer tendencies plus pair effects
results.note: Both sources of bias are present.

results.name: Relationship impressions overwhelm skill ratings
results.note: This deliberately tests the feared collapse toward average. Reviewer calibration cannot recover information absent from the answers.

results.name: Real technical improvement
results.note: Alice improves from 2.1 to 4.3 stars during the last four weeks.

results.name: Real technical deterioration
results.note: Alice deteriorates from 4.3 to 2.1 stars during the last four weeks.

results.name: Occasional extreme answers
results.note: Two percent of skill answers are independently replaced by 1 or 5 stars.

results.name: Everyone uses a harsher scale
results.note: A shared −0.8-star bias has no external anchor; relative calibration cannot identify it.

results.name: Sparse and overlapping evidence
results.note: Only three weeks of answers; half of the skill answers are unobserved.
